#set up dictionary
MergedHDict = {} # empty list for each file(date) in the directory
for filename in MergedHfilelist: # use every name in MergedHfilelist
    MergedHDict[filename] = {} # make a new dict within the main dict for the specific date
    with h5py.File(MergedHorizontalpath+'//'+filename, "r") as f: # reads in the netCDF file as f, which becomes a dictionary with data variables as keys
        MergedHVars = list(f.keys()) # creates list of variable names in the specific file
        for variable in MergedHVars: # loop over variables in list
            MergedHDict[filename][variable] = pd.DataFrame(f[variable][()]) # creates a pandas dataframe for each variable. Example: MergedHDict['Feb 05 2020.nc']['CONCENTRATION'] would be the dataframe for CONC extracted from filename "Feb 05 2020.nc"
MergedHDict['Feb 05 2020.nc']['CONCENTRATION'] # rows are the 42 vectors representing bins, columns are seconds, Z is conc data in #/m4

#sizebins is the endpoints for each bin in the size distribution products for this dataset in particular. hardcoding it was the easiest way here. units in micrometers(um). I do this because each bin is represented by a vector in the raw dataset, and a variable for the actual bin ranges was not provided for this particular dataset, so I had to find them in the metadata for the files.
sizebins = [20.0, 40.0, 60.0, 80.0, 100.0, 125.0, 150.0, 200.0, 250.0, 300.0, 350.0, 400.0, 475.0, 550.0, 625.0, 700.0, 800.0, 900.0, 1000.0, 1200.0, 1400.0, 1600.0, 1800.0, 2200.0, 2600.0, 3000.0, 3400.0, 3800.0, 4200.0, 4600.0, 5000.0, 6000.0, 7000.0, 8000.0, 9000.0, 10000.0, 12000.0, 14000.0, 16000.0, 18000.0, 20000.0, 25000.0]
sizebins = [x/1000 for x in sizebins] # converts um to mm
sizebins = np.array(sizebins, dtype=float) # convert list of sizebin endpoints to array for pandas
sizebins

#create a dict that stores converted time ranges for each date. the files use "seconds after midnight" as a time index, I convert that to datetime here and store it in a new pandas dataframe.
timerange = {}
for filename in MergedHfilelist:
    df = MergedHDict[filename]['time'] # assign time dataframe to arbitrary df
    df.columns = ['Seconds'] # renaming the singular column in this dataframe to "Seconds"
    df.index = df['Seconds'] # replace current index values with values from the time column.
    df.index.name=None # remove index name.
    df.index = pd.to_datetime(df.index, unit="s") # convert index to datetime leaving the singular column as seconds after midnight.
    MergedHDict[filename]['time'] = df # reapply the new time variable dataframe to the old one, with datatime as the index and seconds after midnight as the only column.
    timerange[filename] = df.index # assign every datetime index to this dict that uses filenames as keys.
MergedHDict['Feb 05 2020']['time']

#adjusting the 'CONCENTRATION' dataframes. there are other variables for each file such as IWC, MMD, MND, ect... but this is all we need to plot CONC.
for filename in MergedHfilelist:
    df = MergedHDict[filename]['CONCENTRATION']
    df = df.replace(-999.0, 0) # change null values to 0 because 0 indicates no data with size distributions
    df = df/1.0e8 # convert Z-data concentration values from #/m4 to #/cm4
    df.index = sizebins # set bins on the Y axis to our custom bin endpoints
    df.index.name=None # remove index name for conciseness 
    df.columns = timerange[filename] # set time range on the X axis to the converted datetime range
    df = df.T # transpose dt get time on Y axis
    MergedHDict[filename]['CONCENTRATION'] = df # reassign df

#plotting CONC data for each date using pcolormesh
for filename in MergedHfilelist:
    CONCdf = MergedHDict[filename]['CONCENTRATION'] # assign arbitray variable to conc dataframe
    CONCdf.columns = (CONCdf.columns).astype(float) # converts the column names (bin endpoints) to float so the dependent axis can be plotted

    plt.style.use('tableau-colorblind10') # figure style
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12.5, 9)) # assign subplots to fig and ax
    fig.tight_layout(pad = 8.5) # pad edges of figure
    cmap = cmr.get_sub_cmap(cm.gnuplot2.copy(), 0, 0.9) # make copy of colormap to alter it. use cmr.get_sub_cmap to reduce the color range of the cmap
    cmap.set_bad(color='white') # set 0 to white shading

    #dropped last row/column of data to fit shading scheme. lognorm shades logarithmically. plot data using loop variable. iloc = select by numbers. loc = select by name.
    CONCplot = ax.pcolormesh(CONCdf.columns, CONCdf.index, CONCdf.iloc[:-1,: -1], shading='flat', norm = mpl.colors.LogNorm(), cmap = cmap)

    cb = plt.colorbar(CONCplot, shrink=1, aspect=25, location='right', ax=ax) # add colorbar
    cb.ax.set_title('#/cm⁴', pad=15, fontsize=10.5) # use cb object to set colorbar title
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%I:%M:%S %p')) # format datetime Yaxis to leave off Y m D 

    #need to figure out how to make this dynamic
    ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MinuteLocator(interval=15)) # number of ticks using a datetime locator

    ax.tick_params(axis='y', which='major', labelsize=7.5, grid_linewidth=2, rotation=22) # Y tick labels
    ax.set_title(f"Number Concentration for %s" % filename, pad=13.5, fontsize=15, fontweight="bold") # sets title for the singular subplot
    ax.set_xlabel("D(mm)", rotation=0, labelpad=8) # X name
    ax.set_ylabel("Local Time", labelpad=12.5) # Y name
    ax.set_xscale('log') # logarithmic bin width scale
plt.show()
